title: add recursive trace-linking and compact token-cost histograms for streaming responses
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Long streaming responses and multi-model fallbacks produce disconnected traces and duplicated token cost attributions. This PR introduces a lightweight recursive trace-linking layer plus a compact, slabbed histogram format for per-invocation token-cost that is cheap to emit and easy to aggregate. Goals: 1) join partial/continued streaming traces into a single logical invocation for accurate latency/cost SLOs; 2) emit a low-cardinality, quantized token-cost histogram per invocation to surface tail cost patterns without exploding cardinality; 3) keep runtime overhead under 2% P50 and avoid added high-cardinality labels. Design: - Recursive trace-linking: each streaming chunk now references an ancestor invocation_id and a small link vector (up to 3 ancestor edges). The agent runtime synthesizes a single root span when the final chunk arrives or after a configurable timeout. Link vectors are encoded as short stable IDs to avoid tagging high-cardinality tenant/model names. - Compact slabbed histograms: per-invocation histogram represented as 8 fixed-cost slabs (0-8 tokens, 9-32, 33-128, 129-512, 513-2k, 2k-8k, 8k-32k, 32k+). Hist counts are emitted as an 8-byte base64 payload on a single metric line (metric: redwood.invocation.token_cost_hist) with labels {model_variant, route, tenant_tier}. This keeps metric series low-cardinality while enabling rollups and percentiles. - Backwards compat: Existing token-level metrics (redwood.invocation.token_cost as a gauge/counter) are still emitted for compatibility; ingestion pipelines will use the new histogram when available. - Rollout plan: feature-flag default off; enable for 10% traffic via routing policy then 100% after 2 weeks of monitoring. - Telemetry sanitization: stripped user-provided keys, no PII in link vectors. Implementation summary: runtime (go) changes to span manager, emission sink adapters, and agent protobuf for link vector; metrics ingestion service decoding + rollup job to materialize p50/p95/p99 from slabs. Testing: unit tests for encoder/decoder, e2e synthetic stream scenario, staging rollout with synthetic cost anomalies, load test to confirm <2% latency overhead. Links: Linear ENG-9421 for streaming traces, ENG-9750 for compact histograms. Checklist: - [x] design doc (doc/telemetry/recursive-linking.md) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] load test results attached - [x] telemetry deprecation plan for legacy counters - [x] privacy review completed

review_thread: Miguel Torres: Can we guarantee the link vector doesn't reintroduce high cardinality for multi-tenant deployments? Response (Asha): link vector uses stable short ids and we limit depth to 3; added sanitizer that strips tenant-unique metadata. Jae Kim: Please add a metric for 'link_reassembly_failures' so we can alert on missing final chunk. Response (Asha): Added link_reassembly_failures counter and alert in the rollout stage. Renee Wu: ingestion job looks fine but we should document how to backfill histograms for historical dashboards. Response (Asha): Added rollup job that can replay recent 7 days; documented backfill steps in docs. Miguel Torres: +1 after small nits. Jae Kim: Approved. Renee Wu: Approved.
